verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. Finiteness guarantees a nonempty maximal trail; the parity argument at a hypothetical distinct terminal vertex shows that this trail must be closed. If it omitted an edge, connectedness would provide a vertex on the trail incident with an omitted edge. The omitted-edge spanning subgraph has even degree at every vertex because the used incidences of the closed trail occur in arrival-departure pairs. A maximal trail in that subgraph starting at the chosen vertex is therefore a nonempty closed trail, and splicing it into the original closed trail gives a strictly longer trail, contradicting maximality. Thus the original trail traverses every edge exactly once. The statement is self-contained, all hypotheses are appropriately used, and the proof contains no prohibited or unverified references.
